I wrote `src/main.ts` and it passes `typecheck`. I couldn't run it in a browser, so I haven't seen a rendered frame. Brightness, fog density and whether the camera actually moves are untested.

- **Canyon:** the canyon is a closed, winding loop about 130 units in radius, so the flythrough repeats without a seam. Both walls are stacked instanced boxes with sandstone-coloured strata. Each layer sets back by a varying amount and each side has a different number of layers, so the tops are uneven. The floor is a sand-coloured plane with a paler winding riverbed strip and pebbles on it. Boulders sit on the floor and at the base of the walls. Dead shrubs are bundles of thin tilted twigs.
- **Sky and light:**
  - The sky is a gradient from blue-violet at the top to magenta at the horizon, with an orange sun near the horizon and an orange glow band.
  - The sun is a warm directional light at 11° elevation with cascaded shadows, so shadows are long.
  - A hemisphere light and a weak violet fill light stop the shadowed areas from going black.
  - Exponential fog in a mauve close to the horizon colour fades the distant walls.
- **Camera:** it follows the centreline at eye height (2.4 units) with a look-ahead target. It drifts left and right and bobs slightly, with no user input. One lap takes 110 seconds. Per frame it calls `app.camera?.setPose`. The pose controller is on by default, but if `app.camera` were undefined the camera would stay still.
- **Contract:** it draws into `#app`. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after the app is ready and two animation frames have passed.
